source: Morais O., Cargill C., Parke K. and Barnes T. 2020. Smallholder Pig Production Technicians' Manual. Timor-Leste Ministry of Agriculture and Fisheries, University of Queensland, ACIAR and the TOMAK Program (Australian Aid), Dili.
text: Diarrhea is one of the leading causes of death in piglets still nursing. Common causes: coccidiosis (usually appears 7–14 days old, worse with poor hygiene), whipworm (from around 6–7 weeks, may be blood-stained), and E. coli bacteria (often within the first 24–48 hours, worse in piglets that didn't drink colostrum; can cause rapid death and severe fluid loss). Prevention centers on housing and nutrition: provide a warm, dry, draught-free creep area (extra light/heat helps right after farrowing), keep the farrowing pen clean and dry before birth, avoid sudden temperature changes, keep poultry out of pig pens, and make sure every piglet drinks colostrum within 12 hours of birth. If diarrhea occurs, give electrolytes in drinking water and treat with antibiotics such as neomycin or apramycin (or trimethoprim combinations, penicillin, or oxytetracycline) according to label directions — cephalosporins should not be used for this.
caveat: Medication names and dosages are reproduced from the source manual for reference only. Product availability, correct dosing, and withdrawal periods vary by country and should be confirmed with a local veterinarian or extension officer before use.
